events.headline: Webb finds the most distant ring galaxy yet
events.summary: Webb spotted GS18660, a galaxy with a ring of newborn stars, as it was about 2.1 billion years after the Big Bang. A companion moving away at about 425 km/s hints that a smaller galaxy may have punched through its centre.

events.headline: Voyager 1 trims its power use and resumes contact after a brief pause
events.summary: NASA's Voyager team finished swapping three devices for lower-power alternatives in early September. Communications were briefly interrupted around October 18–20 and have been maintained since.

events.headline: NASA asks industry how to boost, service or retire Hubble
events.summary: NASA issued a Request for Information on October 29 seeking industry interest in raising Hubble's orbit, servicing it, or bringing it down in a controlled re-entry. Hubble has sunk by more than 30 km since its last boost in 2009.

events.headline: A rose-colored Sahara rock is one of the oldest Mars meteorites
events.summary: A NASA-funded study in Science reports that Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara in 2022, formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Zircon crystals dated the rock, and it shows signs of alteration by early water.

events.headline: Roman Space Telescope enters science commissioning, 'fully functional'
events.summary: After checkout of the observatory and its main instrument, NASA says Roman can guide, expose and slew between targets, and tests in crowded star fields and dusty nebulae went well.

events.headline: NASA lays out how SpaceX and Blue Origin landers will reach the Moon for 2028 missions
events.summary: SpaceX will aggregate propellant across tanker Starships in orbit, while Blue Origin will skip propellant transfer and use three transfer stages. Landers and Orion will no longer meet in a near-rectilinear halo orbit.

events.headline: NASA ends Swift's science mission after 22 years; uncontrolled re-entry expected within weeks
events.summary: Swift made its final observation on Oct. 20 after atmospheric drag pulled it below 171 miles (275 km), too low to hold steady on targets. A $30 million rescue attempt by Katalyst's LINK spacecraft was called off after control problems.

events.headline: NASA says Artemis II's heat shield performed as expected, with 9 char-loss spots versus 103 on Artemis I
events.summary: After Navy diver imagery, inspections and X-ray scans, NASA says Orion's heat shield matched pre-flight predictions at about 39 times the speed of sound and above 4,000°F outside. A shorter downrange trajectory cut cracking and char loss r…

events.headline: Falcon 9 launches Bandwagon-5: SpaceX's Starfall capsule, Varda W-7 and 30 other payloads
events.summary: After a weather scrub on Oct. 19, SpaceX launched the rideshare on Oct. 20 from Cape Canaveral with 32 payloads, including Starfall, a Varda capsule carrying a cancer-drug experiment, and Portal Space Systems' 260 kg Starburst-1.

events.headline: Euclid finds its first comet, C/2026 S1, while hunting for galaxies
events.summary: ESA's Euclid telescope turned up a comet in images taken Sept. 16–24; University of Helsinki PhD student Mikko Pöntinen's software flagged a streak, and it sits about 1.3 billion km away with a fuzzy cloud suggesting it is shedding dust an…

events.headline: Webb sees water clouds thicken and thin on the cold brown dwarf WISE 0855
events.summary: A University of Arizona team led by Brittany Miles took a JWST spectrum of WISE 0855, a brown dwarf about 7.5 light-years away, every 15 minutes for 11 hours. They saw high-altitude clouds change in thickness and convection cycles deeper d…

events.headline: Webb pins down the host of the most distant fast radio burst yet, 10.6 billion light-years away
events.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers identified the host galaxy of FRB 20240304B, a burst first detected by South Africa's MeerKAT in March 2024. The host sits at a redshift of 2.148 (about 10.63 billion light-years by NASA's…

events.headline: SPHEREx's first look at 37 nearby brown dwarfs spans 2,200 °C to below freezing
events.summary: NASA's SPHEREx telescope measured the brightness of 37 nearby brown dwarfs in 102 colours, covering the full brown-dwarf temperature range from about 2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius. Only a few dozen brown dwarfs have been studied in det…

events.headline: NASA and the Energy Department sign a pact on space nuclear power and propulsion
events.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed a memorandum covering nuclear fuel, testing, launch integration and a lunar surface reactor; it takes effect November 1. NASA's stated plan includes sending the nuc…

events.headline: Crew-12 splashes down off California after 237 days in orbit
events.summary: The Dragon "Freedom" landed in the Pacific off Los Angeles at 11:34 a.m. EDT on October 8 with Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, ESA's Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos's Andrey Fedyaev. NASA says the crew travelled more than 100 million miles and co…

events.headline: A cargo Dragon carries the space station's final roll-out solar arrays to orbit
events.summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 launched the CRS-35 resupply mission from Cape Canaveral on October 13 with about 6,300 pounds of cargo, including the last two Roll-Out Solar Arrays and gear for more than 40 science studies. Docking was planned for abou…
